title: Ducks, Oilers and a Bruins-sized buzz: the week around the NHL
dek: Cutter Gauthier scored eight goals in four games, Connor McDavid's streak hit 17, and Kucherov and Hellebuyck dominated the headlines.
text:
Cutter Gauthier of the Ducks had the week's most eye-catching line: eight goals and nine points in four games, with two hat tricks, one on Nov. 1 and another on Nov. 3. Anaheim has won four straight, outscoring opponents 21-14, and the nuance matters. Expected goals, the quality of chances a team creates, put the Ducks at 52% of the share over that run. They scored 21 goals on 12.8 expected, so finishing is doing a lot of the work. Gauthier's own chances add up to 2.1 expected goals, against the 8 he scored. We'd enjoy it and not bank on it. With only about 17 games played, short runs are mostly noise.

## Who the league is talking about

The loudest names were not scoring. Nikita Kucherov drew 30 headlines from 12 outlets this week. Sportsnet ran "The Kucherov Calculator: Why Lightning are playing the long game," and Yahoo Sports reported "Maple Leafs told to explore Lightning's Nikita Kucherov after trade request." Sean Gentille of The Athletic posted a Power Rankings piece asking what Kucherov "would do for every team's Net Rating and overall outlook." Tampa Bay, for its part, has points in five straight (3-0-2) and held 53% of the expected goals in that run, so the team is playing well around the noise.

Connor Hellebuyck, listed with New Jersey, also drew 30 headlines. ESPN's headline had him citing "'challenging circumstances' among reasons for trade ask." Our data can add a little context: New Jersey's goaltending has been the weaker unit this season at minus 5.4 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie or team saves compared with what the shots called for), against Washington's plus 4.7.

Dylan Larkin pulled 45 headlines from 18 outlets, the most of anyone. The Hockey News headline read "Bruins Linked To Larkin And Edvinsson," and The Hockey Writers wrote about a "Hidden Advantage in Dylan Larkin's Contract." That is rumor material, and the data here doesn't speak to it.

McDavid drew 30 headlines too. The Times of India asked "Why Connor McDavid's contract negotiations sparked major NHL debate." His point streak now stands at 17 games (10 goals, 34 assists). Our numbers say to expect some cooling: he has 10 goals on 7.1 expected, shooting 22% (16% last season). The same goes for teammates Leon Draisaitl (14 goals on 9.5 expected) and Evan Bouchard (10 goals on just 3.4 expected). Edmonton sits fourth in points at 25 anyway, but that finishing rate rarely lasts.

## The week's best and strangest games

Game of the week was NJD 5, STL 4 in overtime on Nov. 5. New Jersey carried 6.59 expected goals to St. Louis's 4.04, and simulating every shot over and over, the Devils win that game 83% of the time. Anthony Mantha was the star.

The biggest steal came on Halloween: BUF 3, LAK 2, with Tage Thompson the star. Buffalo created 2.59 expected goals to Los Angeles's 3.31, and the Sabres deserved the win only 28% of the time. Toronto got the opposite treatment on Nov. 3, losing 3-2 to Utah. The Mammoth created 4.12 expected goals to 1.72 and deserved to win 87% of the time, with Clayton Keller the star.

The least likely goals of the week: Simon Benoit's slap shot for Philadelphia against the Rangers had a 0.3% chance of scoring. Kyle Connor's power-play snap shot against Montreal was 0.5%, and Danila Yurov's wrister against the Flyers was 0.6%.

## Who owned the week

Beyond Gauthier, Beckett Sennecke posted nine points, mostly on assists (2 G, 7 A), and Leo Carlsson had eight. Logan Cooley, Adrian Kempe and Jason Robertson each had a hat trick as well.

In goal, Minnesota's Jesper Wallstedt faced 76 shots over three games, allowed 4 goals and posted a .947 save percentage, saving 4.7 goals more than expected. That is real, because it rests on a large number of shots. At the other end, Washington's Logan Thompson allowed 8 goals on 39 shots (.795), which cost the Capitals 3.7 goals compared with expected.

Some skaters can feel unlucky. T.J. Hughes of Colorado piled up 2.2 expected goals in four games with none to show for it, and J.T. Miller of the Rangers had 2.2 across three games. Over the longer view, Pavel Dorofeyev (NYR) has 5 goals on 7.5 expected, and Michael Rasmussen (DET) has 1 on 3.9, so both are due for more.

## Trending up, trending down

New Jersey went 2-0-0 and took 62% of the expected goals. Nashville and Boston each went 3-0-0. At the other end, San Jose went 0-4-0, outscored 18-5, with 39% of the expected goals, a collapse the chances confirm. Vancouver went 0-3-0 and sits last in the standings at 3-14-1, and Chicago is winless in five (0-4-1) with 37% of the expected goals. Carolina leads the league with 28 points, ahead of Minnesota at 27.

## Milestones and moves

Patrick Kane reached 900 career assists and Mikko Rantanen 800 career points. Kirill Kaprizov hit 500 career points, and Jaccob Slavin and Phillip Danault each played their 800th game. Lars Eller reached game number 1,200.

On the transaction wire, Seattle and Nashville swapped Shane Wright and Matthew Wood, one for one. Their 5-on-5 chance share is identical (47%), which makes the swap a quiet one on paper. Washington acquired goalie Remi Poirier from New Jersey for a 2027 seventh-round pick.
